gist_written_for_this_record: third statement: the ESO does not itself generate electricity, and the root cause did not lie with the ESO's system; it describes a rare event in which two big generating units, a gas plant and an offshore wind farm, were lost almost at the same moment (time given as 16.54); other generators raised output, but not enough, so a backup protection scheme disconnected selected demand; the DNOs were given the all clear within 15 minutes; reports that DNOs had reconnected all demand by 17.40.

gist_written_for_this_record: next-day notice: after Friday's disruption, trains and crews ended the day out of position, so more cancellations were expected from crew shortages, mainly on routes from Moorgate and King's Cross; Thameslink no longer affected by Friday's power problems; again attributes the cause to a 'UK Power Network' failure across London and south-east England, which it says also affected airports.

gist_written_for_this_record: fourth statement: says the industry must understand both the cause and why the power cut disrupted services so widely, especially transport; welcomes the government's commissioning of the E3C review and promises to work with it; says the ESO had begun reviewing its own response internally and was working with Ofgem, local networks and the generators involved.

label: E36
gist_written_for_this_record: statement on frequency: rejects media reports of earlier near misses or early warnings of similar incidents; calls the event highly unusual and unprecedented in ten years; says that until that Friday the system had stayed within the safe frequency limits agreed with Ofgem; interim findings to be reported to Ofgem that week.
